problem: "a very thin laminar sublayer ... carries almost all the velocity drop from zero to the free stream" is wrong. With the chapter's own numbers (u* = 0.67 m/s, U = 15 m/s), the velocity at the top of the viscous sublayer (y+ ≈ 5) is u ≈ 5u* ≈ 3.4 m/s, about 22 % of U; even at y+ ≈ 12 it is about 8 m/s, roughly half of U. Most of the velocity rise to U happens in the outer turbulent part, not in the sublayer.
fix: "Even then, a very thin laminar sublayer clings to the wall. It holds only about a fifth of the velocity rise from zero to U, but there the gradient is steepest and the whole wall shear passes through viscosity."

where: Section 2, definition of the sublayer vs the formula δs ≈ 11.6ν/u*
problem: The chapter defines the viscous sublayer as y+ below about 5, but the formula δs ≈ 11.6ν/u* gives the height where y+ = 11.6 — the top of the buffer layer, not y+ = 5. A student who checks y+ = δs u*/ν gets 11.6 and concludes the two statements contradict each other. With y+ = 5 the sublayer here would be 0.11 mm, not 0.26 mm.
fix: State the convention once: "Textbooks quote the sublayer edge either at y+ ≈ 5 (purely viscous part) or at y+ ≈ 11.6, where the linear law meets the log law; the common engineering formula δs ≈ 11.6ν/u* uses the second convention. With the first convention δs ≈ 5ν/u* = 0.11 mm here."

problem: The values 7.1 mm and 41 mm come from x = 2 m and ν = 1.5×10⁻⁵ m²/s, but neither x nor ν is given here, so the numbers cannot be reproduced from the formulas shown.
fix: "At x = 2 m with ν = 1.5×10⁻⁵ m²/s (so Rex = 2×10⁶), the laminar estimate is 7.1 mm and the turbulent estimate is 41 mm."

where: Worked example steps 3, 5, 7; quiz Q1, Q3, Q5

where: Worked example step 5 and Section 2 formula u* = U√(Cf/2)
problem: Cf = 0.072/Re<sup>1/5</sup> is the mean skin friction coefficient for the whole plate, while u* = U√(Cf/2) needs the local Cf at the station where the sublayer is being found. Using the mean value at the trailing edge overstates the local wall shear (local c<sub>f</sub> ≈ 0.0576/Re<sub>x</sub><sup>1/5</sup> = 0.00316, giving u* ≈ 0.60 m/s and δs ≈ 0.29 mm).
fix: Either add one line saying the mean Cf is used here as an approximation for the local value, or use the local relation c<sub>f</sub> = 0.0576/Re<sub>x</sub><sup>1/5</sup> = 0.00316, u* = 0.60 m/s, δs = 0.29 mm.
